The position is part of the Inria International Relations Department Postdoctoral Campaign 2026 and aims to support an ongoing collaboration between Inria Saclay and the University of Waterloo. The project builds on our recent work on collaborative visualization, including a joint CHI 2026 paper on challenges in synchronous and remote collaboration around visualization [1], as well as the MERCADO workshop series on communication around data [2].

The topic is centered on collaborative visualization: how people use visual representations to analyze, discuss, communicate, and build shared understanding around data. The selected candidate will be encouraged to shape their own research direction within this space, in dialogue with the Inria Saclay and University of Waterloo teams. Possible directions include, for example, collaborative visual analytics, data storytelling, visualization for situation awareness in control rooms, asynchronous revisitation of collaborative analysis, situated or place-based storytelling, immersive or multimodal interaction, and AI-assisted collaborative visualization.We welcome candidates from various and diverse areas such as:

• Human-Computer Interaction
• Information Visualization / Visual Analytics
• Computer-Supported Cooperative Work
• Data storytelling
• Immersive analytics / AR / VR
• Interaction design
• Qualitative, empirical, or mixed-methods user research

The position will be hosted by the ILDA team at Inria Saclay (
), with expected collaboration and research visits with Matt Brehmer and his group at the University of Waterloo (

), in accordance with Inria mobility rules.

Practical information

• Location: Inria Saclay, France
• Duration: 12 to 24 months
• Gross salary: 2788 EUR/month
• Expected start date: between November 1, 2026 and January 1, 2027
• Application deadline: June 7, 2026
• Final funding decision by Inria DRI/DGDS: July 3, 2026

Eligibility

Candidates must have completed a PhD before the start of the contract and must have defended their PhD no more than three years before the contract start date. The position must also represent a scientific environment substantially different from that of the candidate’s PhD and, if applicable, from their current position. International mobility is strongly encouraged.
